products.title: Buggy to Cybercab Prints
products.body_html:
“Buggy to Cybercab” captures the moment one era of transportation gives way to another. A family trades literal horsepower for electric power, stepping out of a horse-drawn carriage and into a futuristic autonomous vehicle. Centuries of innovation are separated by a single open door; one ride comes with one horse and a driver, while the other comes with hundreds of horsepower and no driver at all. The technology has changed beyond recognition, but the purpose remains the same: getting people from where they are to where they want to go.

Only 100 are printed & signed. 120 lb cardstock

products.title: MJ Hurricane Winds  Prints
products.body_html:
“MJ Hurricane Winds” captures the world’s greatest entertainer standing against an impossible force. His hair, clothing, and jacket are violently swept backward, yet his feet remain planted as he leans directly into the storm. Clutching his hat to his chest, he appears graceful even in chaos. The hurricane represents more than wind; it symbolizes the pressure, fame, scrutiny, and adversity that surrounded him. Everything is being blown away, but the man himself refuses to move.

Only 100 are printed & signed. 120 lb cardstock

products.title: Niagra Falls Spa Signed  Prints
products.body_html:
“Niagra Falls Spa” transforms one of the world’s greatest natural wonders into one giant hydrotherapy session. After PJ and Jillian experienced the Niagra Falls boat tour together, PJ was inspired to turn the overwhelming mist, force, and chaos of the falls into something playfully relaxing. Lounging beneath the crashing water is a colossal PJ; the giant’s face is the artist’s own self-portrait. Equal parts travel poster, hippy era, mythological fantasy, and New York humor, the piece bridges New York and Ontario with one invitation: Come for the mist, stay for the schvitz.

Only 100 are printed & signed. 120 lb cardstock

products.title: Area 4-1 Signed  Prints
products.body_html:
A blue-collar floor general forged in the streets of New York faces an alien talent equipped with otherworldly size and abilities. One was seemingly built in a laboratory; the other was built through hard work, toughness, and relentless determination. “AREA 4–1” tells the story of grit defeating genetics—and the city’s hometown hero completing a gentleman’s sweep: graciously surrendering one game before sweeping the extraterrestrial threat back into the pavement.

 

personal note- I saw the OG tip at a watch party on Stone Street. After 53 years of waiting, this night made our championship hopes really real. It was "Knicks in 5" & absolute pandemonium. Only thing I could compare it to would be my experience on Bourbon Street when the Saints won the Super Bowl. Very similar vibe, New York on a much bigger scale.  

Only 100 are printed & signed. 120 lb cardstock

products.body_html:

Shot in front of the Woolworth Building—the Cathedral of Commerce, famously paid for in cash—this crop tee sets old-money grandeur against modern-day absurdity. Gothic spires loom. Bureaucracy smirks back.

The graphic mashes up the visual language of the Lottery and the MTA, twisting familiar civic symbols into a blunt, wearable truth: in this city, chaos is policy and luck is a transit line that may or may not arrive. The clash is the point. Reverence meets parody. Power meets punchline.

Cut from 100% cotton, 4oz. fabric, the tee is lightweight and cropped with intent—clean, confident, and unapologetic. It wears like a protest sign you don’t have to explain. Sharp contrast. Sharp message. No filler.

Built for summer streets, courthouse steps, and anyone fluent in New York irony.

  • Lightweight, breathable feel
  • Cropped, feminine silhouette
  • Bold black-and-white graphic
  • Designed to clash—architecturally and culturally

Then it built systems to mess with you.

This piece is one of the top 5 most prized in my portfolio; largely in part to the story behind it. So the following two angles will be provided. 

Artistic angle-

Bronx Bombers is my triple entendre concept dreamt up in 2013, & many drafts later—finished in 2016. When I think of Bronx Bombers, I think of three things: New York Yankees, a WWII bomber jet, & prolific graffiti train writers from the 70s & 80s. This design is representing the concept of all three cooked up into one beautiful, vibrant, colorful & intellectually curious design. This design exudes the confidence of Babe Ruth at bat, fifth inning, World Series 1932—when he called “The Shot” to left center field against the Cubs for his last World Series home run. The jet plane represents the courage & accuracy WWII pilot, Tuskegee Airmen Roscoe C. Brown, when he shot down a 262 jet fighter in 1945. The graffiti trains & subway platform wings are bold like artist ZEPHYR in the early 80’s, with crispy clean execution. The cans spraying are bombs ready to drop into an abyss of artistic imagination.

Personal angle-

The Bronx will always be a special place for me as it was my first destination in 2010, when I arrived on a Greyhound bus bound for Port Authority from Biloxi, Mississippi. Javier, born & raised on 183rd & Southern Boulevard, greeted me at 5:30am & took me & my suitcase straight to his (father’s) apartment in The Bronx. The projects of 183rd is where I stayed on my first visit of 11 days. It had a lasting impact on me, & I will always appreciate The Bronx for hosting me on my first visit to New York (I moved to New York a mere 10 weeks later & never left.)

“Bronx Bombers” inspiration came from a love of my experiences from my first impressions of New York. I almost exclusively created this design while hustling my art in the subway tunnels of the L train, its platforms, & the 6 train, & its platforms. This design was a great challenge because the concept of this triple entendre was easier said than done when it came to manifesting, & it took many drafts over many weeks to complete. Three years to be exact, & it took sketches with pencil, ink, water color, & digital sketches. Would the plane be flying to the side? If so, how do I express the graffiti element, a bomber jet bombing graffiti? & many other questions were posed in the brainstorming sessions over the course of the process. In the end, I found a design I was finally content with, & released it in 2016. There must be a time when you as the artist says—“that’s it.” But the time & struggle paid off, as it is & will always be one of my top personal favorite designs of my life.

In the late 1800s, Jules Verne was inspired by a conceptual submarine model at The World's Fair in Paris, France. This inspired the creation of his novel Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea. One such interpretation emerged when I moved to New York City and spent time selling his work in subway stations. On a stormy night aboard the L train from Manhattan to Brooklyn, as the subway car rocked violently beneath the East River, I was struck by the idea of merging Verne’s classic tale with the modern New York City subway system. Imagining a submerged subway network powered by an innovative submarine system, I envisioned the L train-submarine battling a giant squid as it emerged into the East River. This creative fusion of past and present, born from a moment of inspiration, allowed me to bring a unique artistic concept to life. Only New York could’ve inspired this.
